_metadata.independence: Apart from the brief, I read only x15-re-input.json and no other file, repository content, web page or API.

hints.reason: AMAZON via Wonder Woman's name Diana (an Amazon princess of Themyscira); PRINCESS via Princess Diana of Wales; two famous Dianas, and Wonder Woman alone even covers both.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent two-Dianas clue; lines are accurate.

hints.reason: AWARD via the Academy Award Oscar; TRASH via Oscar the Grouch's trash can; a clean, satisfying double reference.
BALL via dodgeball; RAM via the Dodge Ram pickup; both are instantly familiar names and the verb/brand split gives a nice click.
hints.fix: The Ram pickup was long sold as the Dodge Ram, and dodgeball is the gym-class game.

pairs.pair_note: The explanation's present-tense 'Dodge sells the Ram pickup truck' is outdated (Ram has been its own brand since 2010); the RAM line already words it correctly, so align the explanation with it.

hints.reason: BANG via The Big Bang Theory, where Sheldon is the lead; YOUNG via the spin-off Young Sheldon; both show titles are instantly familiar, so this title-join earns its place.

pairs.pair_note: Title-join, but a very satisfying one for a broad U.S. audience.

hints.reason: BASEBALL via the baseball diamond; HARD via diamond as the hardest natural mineral; a classic clean double meaning.
BELL via the cracked Liberty Bell; TORCH via the Statue of Liberty's raised torch; two iconic American Liberty symbols.
BIRD via the nightingale songbird; NURSE via Florence Nightingale, commonly called the founder of modern nursing.
BOARD via Monopoly the board game; BUSINESS via a market monopoly; a fitting double meaning since the game itself is about business.
BOTTLE via 'genie in a bottle' (idiom and Christina Aguilera hit); WISH via a genie granting wishes; easy but clean.
BUTTON via belly button; JELLY via the Jelly Belly jelly-bean brand; both phrases are instant and the rhyming brand makes it fun.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join, but both halves are instantly familiar.

hints.reason: CANNON via cannonball; POOL via pool balls on a billiard table; both instant, and the cannonball dive into a swimming pool is a hidden bonus link.

pairs.pair_note: Fine as is; the explanation could also mention that a cannonball is a splashy jump into a pool, which ties both targets together more delightfully.

hints.reason: Both CHAIN and MAIL via chain mail, the linked-ring armor; mail alone is the true historic term for that armor, so both sides honestly connect.

pairs.pair_note: The targets form one compound and the hint names what it is; simple but fair, and spotting the two halves on the board is a small satisfying step.

hints.reason: CHECK via checkmate; FRIEND via mate meaning friend; the friend sense is British/Australian usage but universally understood by Americans (and echoed in classmate, teammate, roommate), so I judge it fair.

pairs.pair_note: Second opinion welcome on whether the British/Aussie 'mate' counts against the U.S.-audience rule; I think it is familiar enough.

hints.reason: CHRISTMAS via A Christmas Carol; RICH via Scrooge as the wealthy miser (and Scrooge McDuck); both sides immediate.
CLOCK via the cuckoo clock; NEST via the cuckoo laying eggs in other birds' nests and One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest; both instant.
hints.fix: Cuckoos sneak their eggs into other birds' nests, and the bird's nest also gives its name to One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest.

pairs.pair_note: The NEST line's 'as in One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest' wrongly implies the film is about egg-laying; separate the two facts.

hints.reason: COLOR and WIND both via the Oscar-winning song Colors of the Wind from Disney's Pocahontas; a single-title split, but the song is iconic and the aha is real.

pairs.pair_note: Title-split phrase-join; passes because the song is one of Disney's best known.

hints.reason: COUCH via couch potato; VEGETABLE via the potato itself; easy and clean.
TENNIS via the Wimbledon tournament is instant; CREAM via the strawberries-and-cream tradition is a British custom many U.S. players will not reach from the board without the explanation.

pairs.pair_note: Facts are correct (Wimbledon dates from 1877 and is the oldest tennis championship); the question is only whether the strawberries-and-cream link is familiar enough to Americans. Tennis fans will get it, casual players may not.

hints.reason: EARTH via its rotation on its axis; DAY as the time one rotation takes; a basic science fact that clicks cleanly.

pairs.pair_note: Plain but honest; 'roughly' correctly hedges solar vs sidereal day.

hints.reason: DETERGENT via Tide laundry detergent; SURFING via surfers watching the tide; the ocean side is a touch looser than waves would be, but the brand/ocean split is a nice click.
DOG via the pointer hunting breed; LASER via the laser pointer; a clean double meaning.
DRUM via the conga drum; LINE via the party conga line; both familiar and a fun pairing.
END via omega as the last Greek letter ('alpha and omega'); WATCH via the Omega watch brand (James Bond, Olympic timing); familiar enough and a neat split.

pairs.pair_note: Watch brand is moderately rather than universally known, but well within fair.

hints.reason: TOOTH via a lost tooth placed under the pillow; FAIRY via the tooth fairy's visit to that pillow; a familiar childhood scene that evokes both.

pairs.pair_note: The targets form one phrase (tooth fairy) and the hint is its scene; pleasant and fair.

hints.reason: FIELD via cornfield; SCARECROW via the classic scarecrow in a cornfield (Wizard of Oz); clear, easy scene.
FLY and SOUP both via the classic joke 'Waiter, there's a fly in my soup!'; indirect but instantly recognizable, with a real smile on the payoff.
GIANT via David defeating Goliath; STONE via the sling stone that felled him (and, as a bonus, Michelangelo's marble David).

pairs.pair_note: Strong; 'killed with a single stone' is the standard popular telling (1 Samuel says he prevailed with sling and stone, then beheaded him), acceptable as is.

hints.reason: HEART via the heart as a body organ; INSTRUMENT via the pipe or keyboard organ; classic double meaning.
TARGET via the bullseye at a target's center (and Target's mascot dog Bullseye); HORSE via Woody's horse Bullseye in Toy Story.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; the Target store mascot gives a triple layer.

hints.reason: JELLY via a jelly-doughnut filling; TOOTH via a dental filling; a satisfying double meaning (with a sweet-tooth irony).
LETTER via capital (uppercase) letters; STATE via each state's capital city; clean double meaning.
MIDDLE via Middle-earth, the hobbits' world; RING via Bilbo finding the One Ring; both click for anyone who knows The Lord of the Rings.

pairs.pair_note: Good; MIDDLE is the harder side but Middle-earth is widely known.

hints.reason: MOUNTAIN via Mount Rushmore itself; WASHINGTON via his carved face; easy and accurate.
ORDER via Dumbledore founding and leading the Order of the Phoenix; PHOENIX via his phoenix Fawkes; both sides independently true.

pairs.pair_note: The targets form a book title, but the hint links each side separately; strong for a U.S. audience.

hints.reason: PICTURE via a picture frame; SUSPECT via framing someone for a crime; a crisp double meaning.
PLAY via Shakespeare's Hamlet; TOWN via hamlet meaning a tiny village; an excellent double meaning.
RACE via the relay race; TORCH via the Olympic torch relay; clean and familiar.
ROUND and TABLE both via King Arthur's Round Table; one reference, but it is iconic and finding both halves on the board is satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: The targets form one phrase; the hint is its owner. Fair and familiar; the lines frame the 'no head of the table' point as legend, which is fine.

hints.reason: SHOT via vaccines given as a shot (flu shot); VIRUS via vaccines protecting against viruses like flu and measles; plain but honest on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Straightforward; 'many vaccines' correctly hedges oral and nasal forms.

hints.reason: SOCCER via the goalkeeper, often just called 'the keeper'; ZOO via the zookeeper; a clean two-sense link.
SUBWAY via London's Tube; TELEVISION via 'the tube' / 'boob tube' from old picture tubes; both widely known in the U.S. despite one being London and one dated.

pairs.pair_note: Good; the London Tube is famous enough for a U.S. audience.

hints.reason: TITANIC via Leonardo DiCaprio as Jack; TURTLE via Leonardo, the blue-masked leader of the Ninja Turtles; a delightful two-Leonardos clue.
